recipes.title: Aalach Chutney
method: Heat oil in a pan and add the red chillis, asafoetida, tamrind(raw) and urad daal and saute till the urad daal turns golden brown. Keep aside.
Chop the ginger in small pieces and saute in the same pan till the ginger becomes tender. Add salt. Keep aside and let it cool.
Now combine the masalas and the sauteed ginger in a mixer and grind it coarsely.
The chutney should be in a slightly tight consistency and not very loose.
AALACH CHUTNEY IS READY!!!!!

recipes.title: Ambat Bhaji(Molai Kheere)
ingredients: Molai Kheere(Amaranth leaves/Pigweed)- 2 cups finely chopped(stem can be used)
method: In a pressure cooker, cook the dal with haldi. Smash and keep aside.
Soak the tamrind in water and take out the pulp.
Heat oil in a pan and add methi seeds, mustard seeds, red chillis and asafoetida. After the mustard seeds splutter add the green chillis and saute on low flame.
Add the greens(amaranth leaves/pigweed) and saute till it mixes with the seasoning. Keep aside and let it rest for 5 minutes.
Now add the tamrind water along with salt to the greens & seasoning mixture and cook till the raw smell of the tamrind fades away.
Add the cooked dal to the mixture and let it come to a boil.
Now add the rice flour(previously dissolved in water), mix well and let it come to a boil.

recipes.title: Appeech Kheer
method: Add water to the chiroti rava and knead it into a dough, making sure that the dough is tight enough for frying. Let the dough rest for 4-5 hours.
Boil the milk and divide it in half and keep aside.
Roll the kneaded dough as thin as rotis and cut them into even squares. Fry these squares in ghee till they are crisp and golden brown in color.
Alternatively, you can fry the kneaded dough in the form of pooris(rolled as thin as rotis)
and crumble them later.
Now dump these crisp fries in one half of the milk and let it come to one boil.
Add the remaining half of milk and let it come to another boil or till the fries are cooked and tender. Let it rest for 10 mins.
Add the saffron and the sugar and mix well and let it come to room temperature or till it becomes cool.
Add the cardamom powder and mix well.
The trick lies in properly kneading the chiroti rava dough and rolling it in thin and even slices.
The Appeech kheer is now ready...!!!

recipes.title: Edaach(Narthangai) Gojju
method: Cut the eaade in big sized cubes. Keep aside.
Soak the tamrind in water and take out the pulp & keep aside.
In a pan heat 1 tsp oil &fry the urad dal, coriander seeds, Methi seeds, red chillis till golden brown. Grind these in a powder form.Keep aside.

In a separate pan heat oil and add the mustard seeds, green chillis and asafoetida and saute.Then add the chopped eaade to this seasoning and saute. Keep the pan closed and cook till the eaade is soft and tender.
Boil the tamrind water along with salt ensuring that the tamrind water is slightly thick in consistency.
When the tamrind water starts boiling add granulated jaggery.
Once the jaggery dissolves add the cooked eaade along with the seasoning and cook till 1 boil.
Add the masala powder (point 3) and cook for 10 mins. The gojju should be in semi-solid consistency.
Add the curry leaves.

recipes.title: Gola(Unda) Sambhar
method: Soak the tamrind in water and take out the pulp. The tamrind water should be thin in consistency.
Soak the tur dal in water for a minimum of 1 hour or more.
Drain the tur dal and add the red chillies, green chillies, hing, grated coconut and salt. Grind these in a coarse and tight consistency.
Add rice powder directly to this ground batter and mix evenly. Divide this batter in 80: 20 ratio.
Take the larger potion of the batter and mould it into small balls(gola or unda). Ensure that these balls are NOT pressed tightly.
Then take a pressure cooker tray and grease it with oil. Place the prepared golas in it and pressure cook for 3 whistles. Keep aside.
Add salt & haldi to tamrind water and let it cook for approximately 15 minutes.
Add jaggery to the tamrind water and cook till jaggery dissolves.
Add the golas or undas to the tamrind water and boil till the tamrind water seeps in. (Ensure that the golas are covered by the tamrind water. )
Now add the remaining batter(gola batter) in tamrind water and mix evenly being careful not to break the undas or golas.
On a low flame continue to cook for 10 minutes or till you can smell the flavours. The gravy should only be slightly semi solid in consistency.
In a separate pan heat oil and add curry leaves and mustard seeds and remove when the mustard splutters. Add this to the sambhar.
Add this to the sambhar.
Gola(Unda) Sambhar is ready!!!

recipes.title: Maatoda Bhaji
ingredients: Banana flower-1 flower(optional) OR Cluster beans-1/2 cup chopped(optional)
method: Soak the tur dal with red chillis for 3 hours or more drain and keep ready.
In a blender add the drained tur dal, red chillis, salt, asafoetida and green chillis and ground them coarsely and keep aside.(neither powder nor paste)
Cut the banana flower in very thin shapes and add them to salt water to avoid rancidification. (only if using banana flower)
Heat oil in a pan, add mustard seeds and let them splutter.
Use a spoon or hand mix the coarsely ground mixture with curry leaves and banana flower OR chopped cluster beans.
Now add the mixture to the seasoning (spluttered mustards & oil) and mix till the oil gets slightly separates. Let it cook on low flame on closed lid.
Cook till the mixture becomes soft.
Optionally you can roast it by frying it further.
Be careful to take out the pistil ("chorta") and calyx(scale like outermost petal)
Use either banana flower OR cluster beans at one time.
You can cook the Maatoda without the banana flower or cluster beans too.
The Maatoda is a heavy dish and must be combined with a light gravy.
Delicious MAATODA is now ready!!!!

recipes.title: Methkut
method: Grind the haldi stick and dry ginger 2-3 times using a pestle & mortar(tenchun).
Dry fry all the ingredients on low flame till golden brown. The ginger should smoke slightly at this point.
Remove the ingredients from the stove and let it cool to room temperature.
Grind it to a fine powder using mixer.
Add salt when you add the methkut to the rice and not while making the recipe.
Add methkut powder to hot rice and use sesame oil to mix it for the best taste.

recipes.title: Naringich Salpataach Chutney(Orange Peel Chutney)
ingredients: Orange Peel- 2 medium sized ripe oranges
method: Clean the orange peels, remove the white pith and chop them into small pieces.
Heat oil in a pan and saute the red chillis, asafoetida, tamrind(raw) and the urad dal(optional) for about 2 minutes and keep aside.
In the same pan add oil and saute the orange peels till soft. Avoid browning of the orange peels.
Now grind all the ingredients in a mixer with some salt & Without Adding Water, into a semi- solid consistency.
Orange Peel is slightly bitter in taste. The recipe is a combination of bitter,sour and spicy.
As per requirment the spice levels can be increase or decreased.
The recipe tastes better without urad dal, however, in case you are using few orange peels then using urad dal would increase the quantity.
The chutney can be mixed with rice along with some thoopa(ghee).
Naringich Salpataach Chutney is Ready!!!!!!

recipes.title: Pitla
ingredients: Vegetables-white pumkin,yellow pumkin, cluster beans, sweet potato, bittergourd, jackfruit seeds(smashed), ground nut, raw banana, yam, butter beans(moccha kotai)-1/3 cup
Pappad- 2 medium sized grilled on open fire
method: In a pressure cooker, cook the tur dal with haldi. Smash and keep aside.
Pressure cook all the vegetables. Partially smash them and keep aside.
Soak the tamrind in water and take out the pulp.
Boil this tamrind water along with salt on a low flame.

Meanwhile, on a separate pan heat oil and fry the urad dal, pepper, red chiilis, coriander seeds, and asafoetida. Once fried, let it cool down then add them to a blender along with fresh coconut. Ground them to a smooth paste.
Add this ground paste to the boiling tamrind water.
Add the vegetables to the mixture and let it come to one boil.
Add the cooked tur dal and mix well. Add required amount of water to bring it to a thick gravy consistency.
For Seasoning:
Fry mustard seeds in oil till they splutter.
Add this to the gravy along with curry leaves.
Add broken grilled papad on top of the pitla right before serving.
Tasty welcoming pitla is absolutely ready.

recipes.title: Pumpkin Kadi
ingredients: Pumpkin- 1/2+ 1/4 cup; cut into julienne shapes(long)
method: Soak channa dal in water for a half an hour.
Pressure cook the pumpkin and keep aside.
Whisk the sour curd and keep aside.
Grind the soaked channa dal, grated coconut, green chillis and cumin seeds in a fine and smooth paste.
Add salt & turmeric powder to the whisked curd & add the pumpkin and ground paste. Add water as required and mix evenly.
Cook on low flame till it rises to the brim of the vessel and then switch off the flame.
In a pan heat oil, and add the mustard seeds, red chilli and curry leaves and add this mixture to the kadi, when mustard seeds start spluttering, as seasoning.
Pumpkin Kadi is readyyy !!!!!

recipes.title: Daangar
ingredients: 2-3 tbsp urad dal (readymade urad dal powder)
method: Take the urad dal in a bowl and add buttermilk until you get a creamy smooth paste with no lumps.
In a separate pan, heat oil and temper with asafoetida, red chilli, curry leaves, mustard seeds, cumin seeds, and urad dal.
Add the tempering to the urad dal paste, add salt, and mix well.
Serve immediately.

recipes.title: Vangi Dahi Bharit
ingredients: Oil to coat eggplants for roasting
method: Make incisions in the eggplants, coat with oil, and roast until soft and mushy.
Peel the skin and mash the roasted eggplants.
Add cilantro, curry leaves, and salt to the mash.
Add yogurt to the eggplant mixture and adjust salt.
Temper oil with asafoetida, mustard seeds, urad dal, and chillies.
Add the tempering to the bharit, mix well, and serve.

recipes.title: Thona Thona
method: Soak chana dal, toor dal, green chillies, ginger, cumin seeds, and coriander seeds for 30 minutes.
Cook spinach leaves in 2 cups water with a little salt, then mash and set aside.
Add coconut to the soaked ingredients and grind to a fine paste.
In a vessel, mix the ground paste, cooked spinach, buttermilk, salt, and turmeric powder before heating.
Cook on low heat until it boils, then remove from heat.
Heat oil in a small pan and temper with asafoetida, curry leaves, and mustard seeds.
Add the tempering to the dish and serve hot.

recipes.title: Paanak
ingredients: 1 liter water (divided into hot and cold as needed)
method: Heat about 1/2 cup water until hot (not boiling).
Add saffron strands and pounded cardamom; let it infuse for a few minutes.
Stir sugar into the saffron-cardamom water until fully dissolved.
Add the remaining cold water and lime juice.
Mix well, chill, and serve cold or with ice.

recipes.title: Ras Vangi
ingredients: 1/4 kg vangi (eggplant/brinjal), cut into long slices
Lime-sized tamarind ball, soaked and pulp extracted
For spice paste: 2 tbsp chana dal
For spice paste: 1 1/2 tsp urad dal
For spice paste: 1 tsp coriander seeds
For spice paste: 2 tsp khus khus (poppy seeds)
For spice paste: 1/4 tsp methi seeds
For spice paste: 1/2 cup fresh grated coconut
For spice paste: 1 small piece dalchini (optional)
method: Soak tamarind in warm water for 15-20 minutes and extract thick pulp.
Dry roast chana dal, urad dal, and methi seeds until golden.
Add coriander seeds, poppy seeds, cloves, red chillies, coconut, and optional dalchini; fry until aromatic.
Cool the roasted mixture, grind to a fine powder, then grind with a little water to a smooth paste.
Slice brinjals and keep in water to avoid discoloration.
Heat oil, splutter mustard seeds, add brinjal slices, and saute until slightly softened.
Add tamarind pulp and enough water to cover the brinjal; boil until tender.
Add the ground spice paste and simmer 5-10 minutes until flavors combine.
Add jaggery, adjust salt and hing, and garnish with curry leaves.
Serve hot with steamed rice.

recipes.title: Waran Bhaath
ingredients: 1 cup toor dal or moong dal
A handful of chopped coriander leaves
For seasoning: A pinch of hing
For seasoning: 1-2 tsp oil or ghee
method: Wash and cook toor dal or moong dal until soft and mushy, then mash lightly.
Heat oil or ghee in a small pan and splutter mustard seeds.
Add urad dal and fry until golden.
Add hing, chillies, and curry leaves.
Pour the seasoning over the cooked dal.
Add salt, garnish with chopped coriander leaves, mix well, and serve hot.
